lede: US stocks split on November 24: at the 16:00 New York close the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.9%, while the S&P 500 fell 0.5% and the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.5% as technology stocks gave back part of Monday's gains. Analog Devices fell about 18%, the steepest drop among large companies, despite fiscal fourth-quarter results that beat expectations. After the bell, Dell Technologies rose in extended trading after it forecast quarterly revenue of about $56.3 billion, above the LSEG consensus of $53.61 billion.

items.title: Dow rises 0.9% as a chip selloff pulls the S&P 500 and Nasdaq lower
facts: The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose more than 400 points, or 0.9%, at the 16:00 New York close on November 24.
The S&P 500 fell 0.5% and the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.5% at the close, as technology stocks gave back some of the prior session's gains while Nvidia fell.
Anthropic shares fell below their initial public offering (IPO) price during the session, which added to the pressure on technology stocks.
items.why: Money moved out of semiconductors and into health care and consumer stocks, so the price-weighted Dow rose while the tech-heavy indexes fell.

items.title: Analog Devices falls about 18% after it gives a flat first-quarter outlook
facts: Analog Devices shares fell about 18% on November 24, even though the chipmaker's fiscal fourth-quarter results beat expectations.
The company forecast first-quarter revenue of about $4.4 billion and adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $3.82, after fourth-quarter revenue rose 42% to $4.37 billion.
The drop came one day after the shares rose more than 10% in the broad chip rally of November 23.
items.why: A flat outlook from a large analog chipmaker hit industrial and auto chip stocks such as Texas Instruments and Monolithic Power Systems.

items.title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise sinks as it flags thinner artificial intelligence server margins
facts: Hewlett Packard Enterprise fell in extended trading on November 23 after fiscal fourth-quarter results, and the decline continued in the November 24 session.
Fourth-quarter revenue was $14.50 billion and adjusted earnings per share (EPS) $1.43, and the company raised its fiscal 2027 revenue growth outlook to 27% to 35%.
Artificial intelligence (AI) servers sold to large cloud companies carry lower margins than enterprise equipment, and the company expects its operating margin to slip.
items.why: Lower margins on AI server sales are a risk for hardware makers that sell to cloud companies, including Dell Technologies and Super Micro Computer.

items.title: Dell rises after hours as it forecasts revenue above estimates
facts: Dell Technologies shares rose in extended trading on November 24 after fiscal third-quarter earnings and revenue beat expectations.
Dell forecast current-quarter adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $8.40 on about $56.3 billion in revenue, above the LSEG consensus of $7.50 and $53.61 billion.
Infrastructure Solutions Group sales were $41.97 billion against an LSEG estimate of $35.27 billion, and Dell authorized $25 billion in share buybacks.
items.why: Dell's artificial intelligence (AI) server forecast tests demand for the AI hardware that cloud companies are buying, a demand chip and server stocks rely on.

items.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as chief executive after board vote
facts: Nvidia said its board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as president, chief executive officer and director, effective immediately, in a release dated November 23.
Huang resigned earlier in November, when the board named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress interim chief executive and Harvey C. Jones as its first chair.
Jones stays on as chair; the board earlier formed a committee of independent directors to look into the matters around Huang's departure.
items.why: Ends the leadership vacuum at the largest weight in the S&P 500 and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index; governance questions stay open.

items.title: CrowdStrike agrees to buy Zscaler in $43.9 billion stock deal, lifts outlook
facts: CrowdStrike agreed to acquire Zscaler in an all-stock transaction valued at about $43.9 billion, announced with its results on November 23.
Third-quarter revenue rose 28% to $1.58 billion; ending annual recurring revenue (ARR) grew 27% to $6.26 billion, with record net new ARR of $419.2 million.
The company now sees fiscal 2027 revenue of $6.078 billion to $6.084 billion; its guidance excludes the Zscaler purchase.
items.why: The largest cybersecurity deal on record consolidates the sector; it puts other security software stocks and Zscaler holders' exchange terms in focus.

items.title: Medtronic revenue rises 4.5% to $9.4 billion; company keeps full-year outlook
facts: Medtronic's fiscal second-quarter revenue rose 4.5% to about $9.4 billion, or 6.5% on an organic basis; adjusted earnings per share (EPS) were $1.34.
It reaffirmed fiscal 2027 organic revenue growth of 7.25% to 7.75% and adjusted EPS of $5.94 to $6.00, absorbing the separation of its diabetes business.
The MiniMed split-off closed October 15 and added a $2.0 billion gain to reported results; Medtronic also agreed to buy privately held Contego Medical.
items.why: A steady guide from the largest medical device maker sets the tone for medtech stocks after the diabetes unit leaves the group.

items.title: Workday raises subscription forecast to $9.958 billion as quarterly sales rise 11%
facts: Workday's fiscal third-quarter revenue rose 11.2% to $2.705 billion; subscription revenue grew 12.8% to $2.532 billion in the quarter ended October 31.
It raised its fiscal 2027 subscription revenue forecast to $9.958 billion, up 13%, and its adjusted operating margin forecast to 31.5%.
Fourth-quarter subscription revenue guidance of $2.600 billion implies 10% growth, slower than the third quarter's pace.
items.why: Slowing subscription growth in the guide feeds the debate over artificial intelligence (AI) pressure on software-as-a-service stocks.

items.title: Autodesk revenue grows 17% to $2.16 billion; full-year outlook raised
facts: Autodesk's fiscal third-quarter revenue rose 17% to $2.16 billion, 14% in constant currency; adjusted earnings per share (EPS) were $3.20, above its guidance range.
It raised fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $8.360 billion to $8.375 billion and billings guidance to $8.600 billion to $8.650 billion.
Fourth-quarter guidance calls for revenue of $2.220 billion to $2.235 billion and adjusted EPS of $3.21 to $3.26; MaintainX added nearly $33 million.
items.why: A raised outlook from the design software maker is a read-through for engineering and construction software peers.

items.title: HP Inc. revenue rises 9.3% to $16.0 billion; dividend raised
facts: HP Inc.'s fiscal fourth-quarter revenue rose 9.3% to $16.0 billion; adjusted earnings per share (EPS) were $0.83, above its outlook of $0.69 to $0.79, helped by a tariff refund.
Full-year adjusted EPS was $3.33, up from $3.12; the company returned $0.8 billion to shareholders in the quarter and raised its dividend.
The company, led by interim Chief Executive Bruce Broussard, cited continued cost and demand pressures in its fiscal 2027 outlook.
items.why: A cautious 2027 view on memory costs and personal computer demand weighs on hardware makers and their component suppliers.

items.title: Dollar Tree comparable sales rise 4.6%; full-year earnings outlook raised
facts: Dollar Tree's third-quarter comparable store sales rose 4.6%, above its 3% to 4% guidance, on a 3.8% gain in traffic; revenue rose 6.9% to about $5.1 billion.
Adjusted earnings per share were $1.16; consumables comparable sales rose 8.9% while discretionary sales grew 0.4%.
It now sees full-year adjusted earnings of $8.05 to $8.25 per share, including about $0.65 from tariff refunds, on sales of $20.6 billion to $20.7 billion.
items.why: Shoppers shifting to essentials favors discount chains over discretionary retailers heading into the holiday season.

items.title: Eight of 12 Reserve Bank boards sought a higher discount rate in October
facts: The Federal Reserve Board kept the primary credit rate at 4% at its discount rate meetings on October 19 and October 28, according to minutes released November 24.
Eight of the 12 Reserve Banks' boards of directors had recommended raising the rate to 4.25%, Bloomberg reported from the minutes.
The Board's discount rate minutes record the Reserve Banks' recommendations; they are separate from the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) minutes.
items.why: Shows broad Reserve Bank support for tighter policy; relevant to short-dated Treasury yields and federal funds futures pricing.

items.title: Bank of England's Greene says the bank is behind the curve on inflation
facts: Megan Greene, an external member of the Monetary Policy Committee, said on November 24 in London that further tightening is warranted unless the war ends, Bloomberg reported.
Greene said a half-point increase would require clear evidence that energy costs are passing into wages and prices.
The committee voted 8 to 1 in November to raise Bank Rate to 4%, with Catherine Mann voting for a half-point increase.
items.why: Adds to pricing of further Bank of England rate increases; bears on short-dated gilt yields and the pound.

items.title: Former JPMorgan vice chairman Daniel Pinto joins Bank of England's financial policy panel
facts: The Chancellor appointed Daniel E. Pinto as an external member of the Financial Policy Committee for three years from January 4, 2027, the Bank of England said on November 24.
Pinto, a former vice chairman of JPMorgan Chase, replaces Jonathan Hall, who leaves at the end of December after six years on the committee.
items.why: The committee sets UK bank capital buffers and financial stability rules that affect lenders' capital and payouts.

items.title: European Central Bank's Vujčić urges more resilient openness in eastern Europe
facts: European Central Bank Vice-President Boris Vujčić spoke on November 24 at the Conference on European Economic Integration in Vienna.
He said banks in central and eastern Europe are generally well capitalized, with non-performing loans close to historical lows in most countries.
He said public debt in the region is comparatively low but budget deficits have widened, and warned against decoupling from global supply chains.
items.why: Gives no new signal on euro area rates; bears on bank and sovereign credit in central and eastern Europe.

items.title: US consumer confidence jumps to 103.3 in November, highest since January 2025
facts: The Conference Board's consumer confidence index rose 11.4 points to 103.3 in November, from an upwardly revised 91.9 in October.
The Present Situation Index rose 13.7 points to 132.8 and the Expectations Index gained 9.9 points to 83.6.
The reading topped all estimates in a Bloomberg survey of economists, whose forecasts clustered in the low 90s.
items.why: Signals firmer household demand into the holiday season; supports consumer discretionary stocks and pressures Treasury yields higher.

items.title: US readies new Section 301 tariffs on China, EU and more than a dozen others
facts: The administration is preparing tariff increases on China, the EU and more than a dozen other economies, Bloomberg reported on November 24, citing a person familiar.
The duties would rest on Section 301 probes into excess manufacturing capacity begun March 11, 2026, and replace levies the Supreme Court struck down.
The EU, Japan and South Korea could face rates of 15% or less; a US-China trade truce runs to January 10.
items.why: Raises import costs for retailers, automakers and industrials; bears on the dollar, the yuan and European exporters.
